info.title: Bergsmith API
info.description: Session-authenticated browser resources. CSRF is required for mutations. Catalog summaries exclude credential references and connection settings. Maintenance policies and schedules are configuration: edits name the revision they read and are audited with the change.

post.description: Persist a Planning job and return its operation ID. Planning execution and commands follow in BS-018.T2. The same key and typed request return the same operation; a different actor or request conflicts. No publication or execution is implied.

post.description: Record a cancellation request and report what it achieved. Idempotent and monotonic: the first requester and reason are kept. A request after send authorization cannot stop the commit; a terminal job is reported, not changed. Authorization, the cancellation, and its audit record commit together.

503.description: Transient failure; retry the same request

200.description: Cancellation outcome and the job after the request

post.description: Create a fresh-plan retry of a terminal job that did not succeed. The new job links to its source and starts in Planning; no plan, output, or accepted result is reused. The same key and source return the same operation.

503.description: Transient failure; retry the same request

409.description: The source job is not terminal or already succeeded

202.description: Fresh job durably accepted; replay returns the original operation

get.description: Server-sent events for one job, oldest first. Each event's `id` is the job's per-job sequence (1, 2, 3, ...), its `event` is the kind, and its `data` is a JobEvent. Resume with the `Last-Event-ID` header (sent automatically by a reconnecting EventSource) or the `after` query parameter; the header wins. Authorization matches getJob, so unknown and inaccessible jobs are both 404. The stream sends a keep-alive comment every 15 seconds and ends after the event that reaches a terminal state, when the session ends or the caller loses access (checked every 30 seconds without extending the session), or after one hour; reconnect with the last ID seen. A resume point past the job's last event waits for later events, or ends immediately once the job is terminal.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Resume after this sequence; 0 or absent means the start.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last event ID received; takes precedence over `after`.

200.description: Event stream; each `data` line is a JobEvent

400.description: Invalid resume point or query parameter

503.description: Ledger unavailable or stream capacity exhausted; retry the same request

get.description: Reads one page of the namespaces a connection's catalog lists under a parent, or at the top level without one. Requires connections:manage for the connection. Levels are repeated parent parameters, never a dotted path, so a level may contain any character. The catalog is asked for the page size the request names; a catalog that ignores page sizes may answer with more, up to 1000 items. next_cursor continues from the catalog's own page token and is bound to this caller, connection, and parent.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Namespace levels of the parent, outermost first. Omit for the top level.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size asked of the catalog. A catalog that ignores page sizes may answer with more items, up to 1000.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor of the previous page.

409.description: The catalog does not support this operation

503.description: Catalog or discovery capacity unavailable; retry the same request

get.description: Reads one page of the tables of one namespace from the connection's catalog and marks the ones Bergsmith already tracks, with the alias revision a removal must name. Requires connections:manage for the connection. Levels are repeated namespace parameters. A table the catalog places outside the requested namespace is refused rather than reported under it. next_cursor continues the listing; skipped counts identifiers Bergsmith cannot address.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: Namespace levels, outermost first. At least one level.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size asked of the catalog. A catalog that ignores page sizes may answer with more items, up to 1000.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor of the previous page.

post.description: Registers one table, or every table of a namespace, by loading each one from the catalog and recording its alias. Requires connections:manage for the connection. The catalog is read before anything is written, and the aliases and their audit commit together: a request records every table it names or none. A namespace with more tables than one request may record is refused. Registering a name that is registered already is idempotent: the answer carries the identity the first request recorded and created is false. The names belong to the routing they were read with: an edit that lands while the catalog is being read records nothing and returns 409 catalog_connection_changed.

201.description: At least one alias was recorded

200.description: Every named alias was recorded already

409.description: The namespace is too large or holds a name Bergsmith cannot address, a name now holds a different table, or the connection changed while it was read

503.description: Catalog or discovery capacity unavailable; retry the same request

delete.description: Removes the catalog name the caller observed, identified by its alias revision. Requires connections:manage for the connection. The canonical table and its other names stay: jobs and publication evidence still reference the table. Every alias of a table with nonterminal jobs is kept, so a commit is never left without a name to verify it through.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: Namespace levels, outermost first. At least one level.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The revision the browse reported for this alias.

409.description: The alias is not the revision the caller observed, or the table still has nonterminal jobs

patch.description: Deactivates or reactivates a principal. Deactivation ends its sessions, refuses sign-in, and stops future admission and publication, keeps its grants and history, never cancels running jobs, and is refused for the last active administrator. A repeated request changes nothing and writes no audit record.

get.description: Active grants in ascending identifier order. Without a scope filter the page covers the whole organization and requires grants:manage over it; a catalog_connection filter covers that connection and the table grants reached through it, and a table filter covers that table. Both scope filters together are invalid. Revoked grants are kept but never listed.

parameters.name: table

post.description: Grants a role over the organization, one catalog connection, or one table. Requires grants:manage over the target scope, so a connection administrator cannot grant organization-wide access and cannot reach another connection. The grant and its audit record commit together; an identical active grant is refused.

get.description: Terminal jobs of one table, newest first, each with the work its accepted tasks rewrote, plus totals over the requested range. Work that a conflict discarded is reported as discarded_files and discarded_bytes. Requires jobs:read on the table; unknown and invisible tables both return 404. Counts and byte totals are decimal strings.

get.description: What needs attention in the organization, from the execution ledger: terminal jobs whose terminal transition falls in the last day, by outcome and conflict rate; unresolved publications in full and a bounded list of jobs that need attention; visible tables without a sample or with a decision pending by terminal transition; schedule cursors that are overdue plus occurrences folded or skipped in the last day; and registered worker capacity. Job and table figures follow the caller's grants; the schedule and worker sections are null when the caller may not read them.

503.description: Ledger unavailable; retry the same request

get.description: Health findings for one table from its newest metadata-only sample, and the action each finding recommends. An actionable finding carries the prefilled preview that assesses it and the planner's estimate from the current table; an advisory finding says why it cannot run yet. Requires jobs:submit on the table because an actionable recommendation reads the catalog. A table without a sample has null state, no findings, and no recommendation, and the response performs no catalog request. Counters are decimal strings.

409.description: The table's catalog connection is disabled, or its identity or metadata changed

503.description: Transient failure; retry the same request

200.description: Health findings and their recommended actions

credential_ref.description: External credential reference, never a secret. Only returned to administrators.

capabilities.description: The last recorded capability check; only returned to connection managers.

capabilities_checked_at.description: When the last capability check ran; only returned to connection managers.

list_tables.description: Whether the catalog lists the tables of a namespace.

load_table.description: Whether the catalog loads a table's metadata.

commit_table.description: Whether the catalog accepts a commit.

vended_credentials.description: Whether the catalog vends table-scoped storage credentials. The catalog configuration cannot show it; loading a table proves it.

credentials_endpoint.description: Whether the catalog can refresh vended credentials on request.

idempotency_key_lifetime_seconds.description: How long the catalog remembers idempotency keys, in seconds, as a decimal string; null when it advertises no lifetime.

CatalogSettings.description: The operating bounds this connection declares. The summary and the detail carry the same bounds.

maintenance_enabled.description: Whether maintenance may run on this connection's tables. A paused connection stays in service: previews and reads still work, and an unresolved publication is still recovered.

max_execution_seconds.description: How long one job may run on this connection. The coordinator never grants a longer job than this, and the operator keeps the table's inputs readable for the same time.

max_unresolved_publication_seconds.description: How long a publication may stay unresolved before an operator investigates. The bound never resolves a publication.

kind.description: The storage backend this profile serves.

endpoint.description: The endpoint, when the backend names one. User information, a query, and a fragment are removed; an endpoint that is not a URL is left out.

path_style_access.description: Whether buckets are addressed as a path.

project.description: The project that owns the buckets, for GCS.

hierarchical_namespace.description: Whether the account has a hierarchical namespace.

CatalogStorageProfile.description: The storage profiles that apply to this connection. They stay in the coordinator configuration, so they are read-only.

source.description: Whether the connection has profiles of its own or uses the default set.

CatalogUnresolvedPublications.description: The publications of this connection whose outcome is unknown.

overdue.description: Whether the oldest unresolved publication is older than the connection's own bound.

uri.description: Catalog HTTP(S) base URI without user information, query parameters, fragments, or whitespace.

credential_ref.description: Reference to an externally held credential; never supply a secret value.

JobEvent.description: The data of one job event. `reason` is set only for transitions, as the typed state reason; operator cancellation text is never included.

next_occurrences.description: The next cron instants strictly after this response was built, in UTC. A maintenance window can still skip one at admission.

snapshot_id.description: 64-bit snapshot ID as a decimal string, so clients that parse JSON numbers as doubles do not round it.

reason.description: Stable reason for a coalesced or skipped evaluation, such as OutsideWindow. Null for an admitted one.

statistics.description: Newest metadata-only sample, or null when the table has never been sampled.

revision.description: The alias revision. A removal names it, so a delayed removal cannot delete a name that was registered again.

TableAlias.description: One catalog name of a table, with the revision a removal names.

uri.description: Catalog HTTP(S) base URI without user information, query parameters, fragments, or whitespace.

credential_ref.description: Reference to an externally held credential; never supply a secret value.

max_execution_seconds.description: How long one job may run on this connection.

max_unresolved_publication_seconds.description: How long a publication may stay unresolved before an operator investigates.

maintenance_enabled.description: Whether maintenance may run on this connection's tables.

UpdateCatalog.description: Supply expected_revision and at least one editable field. Only supplied fields are validated; omitted legacy values are preserved.

status.description: live renews its lease and may receive grants; draining renews but receives no new grants; expired stopped renewing.

running_attempt_id.description: The granted or running attempt, if any.

name.description: The levels joined with dots, for display.

levels.description: The namespace identifier: levels outermost first.

next_cursor.description: The continuation for the next page, or null when the catalog has no more. It is bound to this caller, connection, and parent.

skipped.description: Identifiers the catalog returned that Bergsmith cannot address, such as an empty level or a name over 255 bytes.

registered.description: Whether this connection already has an alias for the table.

table_id.description: The canonical table, or null while the name is unregistered.

revision.description: The alias row this answer observed. A removal must name it, so a delayed removal cannot delete a replacement.

next_cursor.description: The continuation for the next page, or null when the catalog has no more. It is bound to this caller, connection, and namespace.

skipped.description: Identifiers the catalog returned that Bergsmith cannot address; they are never shown as registrable names.

namespace.description: Namespace levels, outermost first. At least one level.

table.description: The one table to register. Absent registers every table in the namespace.

created.description: Whether this request recorded the alias.

table_id.description: The canonical table the removed name used to reach.

subject.description: Subject within the issuer; sign-in is bound to it.

active.description: A deactivated principal keeps its grants and history but exercises neither.

subject.description: Subject within the issuer, at most 2048 bytes.

GrantScope.description: The organization when both fields are absent or null, otherwise exactly one of a catalog connection or a table.

principal_name.description: Current display name of the principal. For display only; principal_id remains the key.

scope_name.description: Organization, a connection name, or a table name through an alias the caller can see. Null when no visible name exists; never used for authorization.

pool.description: Worker pool named inside the bearer token.
Worker pool named inside the bearer token.

token.description: The only copy of the bearer token. It is never listed or stored.

JobStatistics.description: Detail-only ledger snapshot. Inputs are logical file sizes for accepted tasks; outputs are verified accepted output files. Elapsed time includes planning, queueing and publication. Decimal strings preserve integer precision. Accepted work does not imply publication.

format_version.description: The Iceberg format version, such as `v2`.

partition_specs.description: Every partition spec the metadata retains, oldest spec ID first, including specs only older files reference.

properties.description: The allow-listed table properties that the table sets, by key. Unset properties are omitted, and properties outside the allow-list are never reported.

fields.description: Top-level fields in schema order. A nested type appears in the field's `type` text.

type.description: The field type, with nested field IDs and names, such as `struct<4: x: optional double>`.

default.description: Whether this is the table's default spec.

fields.description: The spec's fields in spec order; empty for an unpartitioned spec.

transform.description: The transform as Iceberg renders it, such as `identity` or `truncate[2]`.

order_id.description: The order ID. Zero is the unsorted order.

fields.description: Sort fields in application order; empty when the table is unsorted.

upper_bound_bytes.description: Exclusive upper bound; null for the final bucket.

partition.description: field=value pairs in partition-field order; empty when unpartitioned.

delete_files.description: Delete files recorded in the partition, of either kind.

snapshot_id.description: Decimal string; null when the table has no snapshot.

oldest_snapshot_age_seconds.description: Whole seconds since the oldest snapshot; null without a snapshot log.

newest_snapshot_age_seconds.description: Whole seconds since the last commit; null without a snapshot log.

latest.description: Newest sample regardless of the requested range.

job_id.description: The Bergsmith job that published the snapshot, when the committing engine recorded one.

properties.description: The committing engine's summary properties, including Bergsmith's own job, publication, and proposal evidence. Per-partition counters (`partitions.*`) are omitted without permission to submit jobs on the table.

elapsed_millis.description: End-to-end time from creation to the terminal state.

output_files.description: Output objects accepted with the tasks' receipts.

delete_files_applied.description: Distinct delete files the accepted tasks applied.

since.description: Inclusive lower bound of the range.

conflict_rate_percent.description: Replanned jobs as a percentage of terminal jobs in the window, one decimal.

never_sampled.description: Visible tables without a statistics sample.

latest_job_attention.description: Visible tables whose newest terminal job in the window replanned or failed.

coalesced_last_day.description: Occurrences folded into a later evaluation in the last day.

skipped_last_day.description: Occurrences refused in the last day.

overdue.description: Enabled schedules whose next due instant has passed.

oldest_overdue_age_seconds.description: Seconds the oldest overdue schedule has waited.

live_sessions.description: Sessions whose lease is current and which are not draining.

memory_bytes.description: Memory the live sessions registered, in bytes.

cpu_millis.description: CPU millicores the live sessions registered.

schedules.description: Present only for callers allowed to manage schedules.

workers.description: Present only for callers allowed to manage workers.

age_seconds.description: Seconds since the publication was authorized, or since the job ended.

oldest_unresolved_age_seconds.description: Seconds since the oldest unresolved publication was authorized.

terminal_jobs.description: Replanned or failed jobs inside the window, by terminal transition.

truncated.description: Whether more jobs need attention than the bounded list shows.

TableHealthFinding.description: One finding at warning or worse, with the measurement and the bound it crossed.

TableRecommendationPreview.description: The prefilled preview request that assesses the recommended action.

TableRecommendationEstimate.description: The planner's estimate for the recommended preview.

TableHealthRecommendation.description: The action that resolves one finding. An advisory recommendation carries only the reason; an actionable one carries the preview and the planner's estimate.

TableRecommendations.description: One table's health and the action each finding recommends. Null state means the table has no statistics sample.
